events.title: Mircea the Elder holds the field against Bayezid I at Rovine
events.description: Mircea the Elder of Wallachia met the invading Ottoman army of Sultan Bayezid I, which heavily outnumbered his own and included Serbian vassals, at Rovine. Though the outcome is disputed, Mircea held the field and Wallachia preserved its autonomy.

events.title: Duke of Buckingham is executed for treason
events.description: Edward Stafford, Duke of Buckingham, was beheaded on Tower Hill after a trial for allegedly plotting against Henry VIII. His fall showed how dangerous royal blood had become under the Tudors.
events.html: Edward Stafford, Duke of Buckingham, was beheaded on Tower Hill after a trial for allegedly plotting against Henry VIII. His fall showed how dangerous royal blood had become under the Tudors.

events.title: Henry VIII's marriage to Anne Boleyn is annulled
events.description: King Henry VIII's marriage to Anne Boleyn, his second wife and Queen of England since 1533, was annulled. The circumstances of her marriage and execution for treason made her a key figure at the start of the English Reformation.
events.html: King Henry VIII's marriage to Anne Boleyn, his second wife and Queen of England since 1533, was annulled. The circumstances of her marriage and execution for treason made her a key figure at the start of the English Reformation.

events.title: Anne of Denmark is crowned queen of Scotland at Holyrood
events.description: Anne of Denmark, who had married King James VI in 1589, was crowned Queen of Scotland at Holyrood Abbey in Edinburgh. Her ceremonial entry into the city, with spectacle, theatre and allegorical tableaux, followed on 19 May.
events.html: Anne of Denmark, who had married King James VI in 1589, was crowned Queen of Scotland at Holyrood Abbey in Edinburgh. Her ceremonial entry into the city, with spectacle, theatre and allegorical tableaux, followed on 19 May.

events.title: Jolliet and Marquette set out to explore the Mississippi
events.description: Louis Jolliet and the Jesuit Jacques Marquette left St Ignace with five companions in two canoes. They travelled down the Mississippi as far as the Arkansas River, mapping it for France.
events.html: Louis Jolliet and the Jesuit Jacques Marquette left St Ignace with five companions in two canoes. They travelled down the Mississippi as far as the Arkansas River, mapping it for France.

events.title: Brokers sign the Buttonwood Agreement on Wall Street
events.description: Twenty-four brokers agreed to trade securities among themselves at a fixed commission. Their pact, traditionally signed under a buttonwood tree, is the origin of the New York Stock Exchange.
events.html: Twenty-four brokers agreed to trade securities among themselves at a fixed commission. Their pact, traditionally signed under a buttonwood tree, is the origin of the New York Stock Exchange.

events.title: Supreme Court strikes down school segregation
events.description: In Brown v. Board of Education the US Supreme Court ruled unanimously that racially segregated public schools were unconstitutional, overturning the 'separate but equal' doctrine in education.
events.html: In Brown v. Board of Education the US Supreme Court ruled unanimously that racially segregated public schools were unconstitutional, overturning the 'separate but equal' doctrine in education.

events.title: Senate Watergate hearings open on television
events.description: The Senate committee began televised hearings into the Watergate break-in and cover-up. Testimony revealed the White House taping system, which led to Nixon's resignation in August 1974.
